source_span: You potentially have a supply shock hurting growth at the same time as the Fed is pushed toward tightening. Not a great backdrop for multiples.
source_chain: Iran/Hormuz escalation drives crude, gas and distillates sharply higher (supply shock) therefore that commodity inflation now pulls front-end yields up too, because markets price a real chance the Fed responds therefore a supply shock hurting growth arrives at the same moment the Fed is pushed toward tightening, a bad backdrop for multiples/stocks; invalidation: if crude, gas and product prices fall, yields stabilize and risk can recover provided NFP/CPI cooperate — if energy keeps rising, the Fed reaction function gets dragged with it and sustained upside gets much harder.
pulse_chain: US-Iran escalation drives Brent, European gas, diesel and gasoil sharply higher (supply shock) therefore that moves bonds: yields rise across the curve because higher fuel costs are now dragging short-dated yields up too, as traders price a real chance the Fed responds (hike odds, Barr) therefore stocks fall, which Goldman's sales desk reads as a supply shock hitting growth at the same moment policy is pushed toward tightening, a poor backdrop for earnings multiples, with sustained upside getting much harder if energy keeps climbing; invalidation: if crude, gas and refined fuel prices come lower, yields can stabilize and risk assets can recover provided payrolls and inflation cooperate — otherwise energy keeps deciding the Fed's next move.
why: The pulse reproduces Privorotsky's exact sequence (energy shock → front-end yields via Fed repricing → growth-hit-plus-tightening squeeze on multiples) and his exact invalidation (energy relief → yields stabilize → risk recovers, conditional on payrolls/inflation), correctly attributed to Goldman's sales desk, just compressed and translated (multiples → "what investors will pay for earnings").
